choice_context: Users are selecting between code completions based on their personal and professional coding values and priorities.
reasoning: The 25 most important unipolar features were selected based on their frequency, distinctiveness, and ability to subsume multiple related themes. Each feature represents a single quality that can be present to varying degrees in a code completion, and they are designed to be distinct and preference-relevant.

dimensions.name: Code Simplicity

low_pole.label: Complex
low_pole.description: Code is verbose, includes unnecessary abstractions, or is difficult to understand at a glance.
low_pole.typical_person: A developer who prioritizes completeness over brevity.

high_pole.label: Simple
high_pole.description: Code is concise, avoids unnecessary complexity, and is easy to read and understand.
high_pole.typical_person: A developer who values minimalism and clarity.

example_contrast.low_option: A solution with nested loops and multiple helper functions.
example_contrast.high_option: A one-liner using built-in functions.

dimensions.scoring_guidance: Rate based on how concise and readable the code is, with 5 being minimal and immediately understandable.

dimensions.name: Modularity

low_pole.label: Monolithic
low_pole.description: Code is tightly coupled, lacks reusable components, and is not easily testable or maintainable.
low_pole.typical_person: A developer focused on quick, one-off solutions.

high_pole.label: Modular
high_pole.description: Code is broken into reusable, testable components and follows separation of concerns.
high_pole.typical_person: A developer who values long-term maintainability and reusability.

example_contrast.low_option: A single function that handles all logic in one place.
example_contrast.high_option: A set of small, focused functions with clear responsibilities.

dimensions.scoring_guidance: Rate based on how well the code is broken into reusable, independent parts.

dimensions.name: Functionality Clarity

low_pole.label: Ambiguous
low_pole.description: Code is unclear in its purpose or how it works, requiring additional context or documentation.
low_pole.typical_person: A developer who is indifferent to readability.

high_pole.label: Clear
high_pole.description: Code is immediately understandable in its purpose and behavior, with minimal need for external explanation.
high_pole.typical_person: A developer who values readability and maintainability.

example_contrast.low_option: A function with unclear variable names and no comments.
example_contrast.high_option: A function with descriptive names and inline comments.

dimensions.scoring_guidance: Rate based on how immediately clear the code's purpose and behavior are.

dimensions.name: System-Level Control

low_pole.label: High-level
low_pole.description: Code abstracts away system-level details and uses high-level libraries or frameworks.
low_pole.typical_person: A developer who prefers working with abstractions.

high_pole.label: Low-level
high_pole.description: Code interacts directly with system resources, files, or hardware, offering fine-grained control.
high_pole.typical_person: A developer who values direct system access and performance.

example_contrast.low_option: Using a high-level file API like `fs.readFileSync()`.
example_contrast.high_option: Using system calls or direct memory manipulation.

dimensions.scoring_guidance: Rate based on how directly the code interacts with system resources or hardware.

dimensions.name: Automation Focus

low_pole.label: Manual
low_pole.description: Code is written for one-time use or requires manual intervention to complete tasks.
low_pole.typical_person: A developer who works on ad-hoc tasks.

high_pole.label: Automated
high_pole.description: Code is designed to be run repeatedly, with minimal or no user intervention.
high_pole.typical_person: A developer who values efficiency and repeatability.

example_contrast.low_option: A script that requires user input at each step.
example_contrast.high_option: A script that runs unattended and logs results.

dimensions.scoring_guidance: Rate based on how much the code is designed for repeatable, unattended execution.

dimensions.name: Web Integration

low_pole.label: Standalone
low_pole.description: Code does not interact with web services, APIs, or HTTP-based systems.
low_pole.typical_person: A developer who works on local or backend-only systems.

high_pole.label: Web-focused
high_pole.description: Code is designed to interact with web APIs, endpoints, or HTTP-based systems.
high_pole.typical_person: A developer who works with web services and RESTful APIs.

example_contrast.low_option: A script that reads from a local file.
example_contrast.high_option: A script that fetches data from a REST API.

dimensions.scoring_guidance: Rate based on how much the code interacts with web-based systems or APIs.

dimensions.name: Security Focus

low_pole.label: Unsecured
low_pole.description: Code does not include security measures like input validation, access control, or encryption.
low_pole.typical_person: A developer who prioritizes speed over security.

high_pole.label: Secure
high_pole.description: Code includes robust security practices such as input validation, access control, and encryption.
high_pole.typical_person: A developer who prioritizes data integrity and user safety.

example_contrast.low_option: A function that accepts user input without validation.
example_contrast.high_option: A function that sanitizes and validates all inputs.

dimensions.scoring_guidance: Rate based on how many security practices are included in the code.

dimensions.name: Error Handling

low_pole.label: Unreliable
low_pole.description: Code lacks error handling, making it prone to crashes or undefined behavior.
low_pole.typical_person: A developer who prioritizes speed over robustness.

high_pole.label: Robust
high_pole.description: Code includes comprehensive error handling and defensive programming techniques.
high_pole.typical_person: A developer who values reliability and stability.

example_contrast.low_option: A function that does not handle exceptions.
example_contrast.high_option: A function with try-catch blocks and fallback logic.

dimensions.scoring_guidance: Rate based on how thoroughly the code handles potential errors and edge cases.

dimensions.name: Testability

low_pole.label: Untestable
low_pole.description: Code is difficult to test due to tight coupling, lack of modularity, or unclear interfaces.
low_pole.typical_person: A developer who does not prioritize testing.

high_pole.label: Testable
high_pole.description: Code is designed with testing in mind, using modular components and clear interfaces.
high_pole.typical_person: A developer who values automated testing and CI/CD.

example_contrast.low_option: A monolithic function with no clear entry points for testing.
example_contrast.high_option: A function with clear inputs and outputs, suitable for unit testing.

dimensions.scoring_guidance: Rate based on how easy it is to write tests for the code.

dimensions.name: User Interaction

low_pole.label: Passive
low_pole.description: Code does not include user interaction or feedback mechanisms.
low_pole.typical_person: A developer who works on backend or batch systems.

high_pole.label: Interactive
high_pole.description: Code includes user input, feedback, or real-time interaction.
high_pole.typical_person: A developer who builds user-facing or real-time systems.

example_contrast.low_option: A script that runs silently in the background.
example_contrast.high_option: A script that prompts the user for input and provides progress updates.

dimensions.scoring_guidance: Rate based on how much the code includes user interaction or feedback.

dimensions.name: Data Processing

low_pole.label: Minimal
low_pole.description: Code does not process or transform data in any meaningful way.
low_pole.typical_person: A developer who works with simple data structures.

high_pole.label: Data-rich
high_pole.description: Code includes complex data transformations, pipelines, or modeling.
high_pole.typical_person: A developer who works with large datasets or analytics.

example_contrast.low_option: A script that reads a file and prints its contents.
example_contrast.high_option: A script that parses, filters, and aggregates data from multiple sources.

dimensions.scoring_guidance: Rate based on the complexity and volume of data being processed.

dimensions.name: Dependency Use

low_pole.label: No dependencies
low_pole.description: Code is self-contained and does not rely on external libraries or frameworks.
low_pole.typical_person: A developer who values lightweight and portable code.

high_pole.label: Heavy dependencies
high_pole.description: Code relies on multiple external libraries or frameworks to achieve its goals.
high_pole.typical_person: A developer who prefers using existing tools over writing from scratch.

example_contrast.low_option: A script using only built-in language features.
example_contrast.high_option: A script using multiple third-party libraries.

dimensions.scoring_guidance: Rate based on the number and importance of external dependencies used.

dimensions.name: Immediate Results

low_pole.label: Delayed
low_pole.description: Code requires setup, configuration, or long-running processes before results are visible.
low_pole.typical_person: A developer who is comfortable with long-term projects.

high_pole.label: Immediate
high_pole.description: Code produces visible results quickly, with minimal setup or configuration.
high_pole.typical_person: A developer who values rapid prototyping and feedback.

example_contrast.low_option: A script that requires installing dependencies and running a server.
example_contrast.high_option: A script that runs immediately and shows output in the console.

dimensions.scoring_guidance: Rate based on how quickly the code produces visible results.

dimensions.name: Educational Value

low_pole.label: Practical only
low_pole.description: Code is focused on solving the problem with no additional explanation or learning value.
low_pole.typical_person: A developer who is only interested in the solution.

high_pole.label: Educational
high_pole.description: Code includes comments, explanations, or examples that help the user learn or understand the solution.
high_pole.typical_person: A developer who values learning and teaching.

example_contrast.low_option: A function with no comments or documentation.
example_contrast.high_option: A function with inline comments and a README explaining the approach.

dimensions.scoring_guidance: Rate based on how much the code includes educational elements or explanations.

dimensions.name: RESTful Design

low_pole.label: Non-REST
low_pole.description: Code does not follow RESTful principles or conventions for API design.
low_pole.typical_person: A developer who is not focused on API design.

high_pole.label: RESTful
high_pole.description: Code follows RESTful conventions for API design, including proper HTTP methods and resource naming.
high_pole.typical_person: A developer who works with web APIs and backend systems.

example_contrast.low_option: An API endpoint that uses POST for all operations.
example_contrast.high_option: An API endpoint that uses GET, POST, PUT, and DELETE appropriately.

dimensions.scoring_guidance: Rate based on how well the code follows RESTful API design principles.

dimensions.name: Database Integration

low_pole.label: No database
low_pole.description: Code does not interact with a database or persist data in any way.
low_pole.typical_person: A developer who works with in-memory or temporary data.

high_pole.label: Database-focused
high_pole.description: Code includes database operations such as querying, inserting, or modeling data.
high_pole.typical_person: A developer who works with persistent data and relational systems.

example_contrast.low_option: A script that stores data in memory.
example_contrast.high_option: A script that connects to a database and performs CRUD operations.

dimensions.scoring_guidance: Rate based on how much the code interacts with a database or persists data.

dimensions.name: File System Interaction

low_pole.label: No file access
low_pole.description: Code does not interact with the file system or handle file operations.
low_pole.typical_person: A developer who works with in-memory or cloud-based systems.

high_pole.label: File-focused
high_pole.description: Code includes file operations such as reading, writing, or manipulating files and directories.
high_pole.typical_person: A developer who works with local or file-based systems.

example_contrast.low_option: A script that uses in-memory data structures.
example_contrast.high_option: A script that reads from and writes to multiple files.

dimensions.scoring_guidance: Rate based on how much the code interacts with the file system.

dimensions.name: Command-Line Focus

low_pole.label: GUI-based
low_pole.description: Code is designed for use in a graphical user interface or web application.
low_pole.typical_person: A developer who works with frontend or GUI-based systems.

high_pole.label: CLI-focused
high_pole.description: Code is designed for use in a command-line interface, with no GUI dependencies.
high_pole.typical_person: A developer who works with scripts, automation, or DevOps tools.

example_contrast.low_option: A web-based form submission handler.
example_contrast.high_option: A command-line script that accepts arguments and prints output.

dimensions.scoring_guidance: Rate based on how much the code is designed for command-line use.

dimensions.name: Real-Time Interaction

low_pole.label: Batch
low_pole.description: Code is designed to run in the background or as a batch process, with no real-time interaction.
low_pole.typical_person: A developer who works with long-running or scheduled tasks.

high_pole.label: Real-time
high_pole.description: Code is designed to respond to user input or system events in real time.
high_pole.typical_person: A developer who works with interactive or event-driven systems.

example_contrast.low_option: A script that runs once and exits.
example_contrast.high_option: A script that listens for events and responds immediately.

dimensions.scoring_guidance: Rate based on how much the code is designed for real-time interaction.

dimensions.name: Scalability

low_pole.label: Limited
low_pole.description: Code is not designed to scale and may break or become inefficient with larger inputs or workloads.
low_pole.typical_person: A developer who works on small-scale or one-off projects.

high_pole.label: Scalable
high_pole.description: Code is designed to handle large inputs, high traffic, or distributed systems efficiently.
high_pole.typical_person: A developer who works on large-scale or enterprise systems.

example_contrast.low_option: A script that processes one file at a time.
example_contrast.high_option: A script that processes files in parallel or uses a queue system.

dimensions.scoring_guidance: Rate based on how well the code is designed to scale with larger inputs or workloads.

dimensions.name: Convention-Driven

low_pole.label: Ad-hoc
low_pole.description: Code does not follow any specific conventions or patterns and is written in a freeform way.
low_pole.typical_person: A developer who prefers flexibility over structure.

high_pole.label: Conventional
high_pole.description: Code follows established conventions, patterns, or frameworks for the language or domain.
high_pole.typical_person: A developer who values consistency and team collaboration.

example_contrast.low_option: A function with inconsistent naming and structure.
example_contrast.high_option: A function that follows PEP8 or other style guides.

dimensions.scoring_guidance: Rate based on how well the code follows established conventions or patterns.

dimensions.name: Declarative Style

low_pole.label: Imperative
low_pole.description: Code is written in an imperative style, with explicit step-by-step instructions.
low_pole.typical_person: A developer who prefers control over execution flow.

high_pole.label: Declarative
high_pole.description: Code is written in a declarative style, focusing on what to do rather than how to do it.
high_pole.typical_person: A developer who values abstraction and readability.

example_contrast.low_option: A loop that manually iterates and modifies a list.
example_contrast.high_option: A list comprehension or functional-style transformation.

dimensions.scoring_guidance: Rate based on how much the code uses declarative or functional programming patterns.

dimensions.name: Object-Oriented Design

low_pole.label: Procedural
low_pole.description: Code is written in a procedural style, with no use of classes or objects.
low_pole.typical_person: A developer who prefers functional or script-based approaches.

high_pole.label: Object-oriented
high_pole.description: Code is written using object-oriented principles, with classes, inheritance, and encapsulation.
high_pole.typical_person: A developer who works with large-scale applications or frameworks.

example_contrast.low_option: A script with functions and global variables.
example_contrast.high_option: A script with classes and encapsulated behavior.

dimensions.scoring_guidance: Rate based on how much the code uses object-oriented design patterns.

dimensions.name: Integration Readiness

low_pole.label: Isolated
low_pole.description: Code is not designed to integrate with other systems, tools, or services.
low_pole.typical_person: A developer who works in isolation or on standalone projects.

high_pole.label: Integrated
high_pole.description: Code is designed to work with external tools, APIs, or services and includes integration points.
high_pole.typical_person: A developer who works in a connected or modular ecosystem.

example_contrast.low_option: A script that does not expose any API or hook.
example_contrast.high_option: A script that includes hooks for external tools or plugins.

dimensions.scoring_guidance: Rate based on how well the code is designed to integrate with external systems.

dimensions.name: User Experience

low_pole.label: Basic
low_pole.description: Code provides minimal user experience, with no attention to interface or feedback.
low_pole.typical_person: A developer who is not focused on user-facing systems.

high_pole.label: Polished
high_pole.description: Code includes user-friendly interfaces, feedback, and clear communication with the user.
high_pole.typical_person: A developer who works on user-facing or interactive systems.

example_contrast.low_option: A script that prints raw data to the console.
example_contrast.high_option: A script that formats output and provides clear user prompts.

dimensions.scoring_guidance: Rate based on how user-friendly and polished the code's interface is.

redundancy_check.correlation_note: Code simplicity and functionality clarity are closely related, as simple code is often clearer.
redundancy_check.resolution: They are kept separate because they can vary independently — a function can be clear but complex, or simple but unclear.

redundancy_check.correlation_note: Modular code is often more testable, but not always.
redundancy_check.resolution: They are kept separate because modularity is about structure, while testability is about design for testing.

redundancy_check.correlation_note: Automation and immediate results can be at odds — automation often requires setup.
redundancy_check.resolution: They are kept separate because they represent different goals — automation for efficiency, immediate results for feedback.

redundancy_check.correlation_note: User interaction and user experience are related, but not the same.
redundancy_check.resolution: User interaction is about input/output, while user experience is about the quality of that interaction.

redundancy_check.correlation_note: Both deal with external systems, but one is about libraries and the other about databases.
redundancy_check.resolution: They are kept separate because they represent different types of external dependencies.
